packages.label: מַלְכוּת וְהַתִּקּוּן — Kingship and Its Repair
packages.reason: This vast cluster orbits מלכות (divine kingship / speech-dimension) as the central concept of Torah #4. Malkhut is the aspect of divinity that can fall into exile (among the nations, into impure letter-combinations, into sin) and must be restored. The mechanism of restoration is ודוי דברים (verbal confession) before a תלמיד חכם, who is a bechina of משה, who is a bechina of אין (nothingness). Malkhut is equated with אותיות (letters of speech), דבר/דברים (words/leadership), ישות (existence), רצונות (divine wills/forms), תמונות (letter-shapes), and bears names like אלהים (divine name of kingship/judgment), יהודה (who confessed), מואב (from whom David came). The תלמיד חכם cluster (פרשת דרכים, אבוקה של אור, שארית, תורה, חלב) forms the positive mechanism of repair. The אש / תורה bridge is critical: Torah is fire from which malkhut originates, while חמימות היצר is the evil fire that pulled malkhut into impurity — both share the nature of אש. Merged into this package: צדיק, גדר, 'ברית מלח עולם' (the tzaddik who protects like a fence and a covenant of salt); צדיק הדור/אם (the tzaddik nurses Israel like a mother with Torah-milk); ישראל/דג (Israel as the fish in the parable of the whale, struggling with impure prayer); מצוה/התחברות (mitzvah = connection/bonding, which reconnects broken bones); 'והולכתי עורים'/הצדיק הורה (the tzaddik guides the blind on the right path); עמוד השחר/צדקה (charity as the dawn that delivers from evil — the second of three approaches to the tzaddik).
merge_notes: Component 9 (צדיק, גדר, 'ברית מלח עולם'): The tzaddik is described as a fence (גדר) protecting Israel's breaches and as an eternal salt-covenant (ברית מלח עולם) preserving against corruption. This is structurally identical to the תלמיד חכם / משה cluster — all three terms describe the same righteous guide who repairs malkhut. Merged by shared nature: the righteous teacher who heals.

Component 10 (צדיק הדור, אם): The tzaddik of the generation is called 'mother' because he nurses Israel with the light of his Torah (Torah = milk). This connects directly to the Torah/תלמיד חכם axis and the pastoral-nursing metaphor of spiritual guidance. Merged by shared nature: the tzaddik as spiritual nurturer.

Component 11 (ישראל, דג): In the Rabba bar bar Chana parable, Israel is compared to fish (דגים) — a neutral metaphor describing the Jewish people as those who elevate malkhut. Since the parable is entirely framed around the malkhut-restoration theme of this Torah, the fish-Israel identity belongs here. Merged by shared narrative context.

Component 16 (מצוה, התחברות): 'Mitzvah' derives from 'tzavta' (connection/bonding) — when one does bundles of mitzvot, the broken bones rejoin. This is a positive repair mechanism parallel to the ודוי/תלמיד חכם pathway. Merged by shared nature: mechanisms of spiritual reconnection and repair.

Component 17 ('והולכתי עורים', הצדיק הורה לו דרך ישר): 'I will lead the blind on unknown paths' = the tzaddik guiding to the right path = explicitly equated with פרשת דרכים (the crossroads / the talmid chakham) in the same proof text. Already adjacent to this package's תלמיד חכם cluster. Merged by shared nature.

Component 18 (עמוד השחר, צדקה): Dawn (עמוד השחר) = tzedakah, which delivers from the 'evil beast and bandits' (evil elements of Chai and Medaber). Tzedakah is the second of the three approaches to the tzaddik described in this Torah. Since the three approaches (seeing tzaddik, giving tzedakah, verbal confession) all function as mechanisms for repairing malkhut, tzedakah belongs in the malkhut-repair cluster. Merged by shared nature: practical mechanisms of malkhut restoration.

packages.label: דַּעַת וְאַחְדוּת — Da'at and Divine Unity
packages.label_en: Unified Consciousness: Knowing Chesed and Din Are One
packages.reason: This cluster centers on דַּעַת (unified knowledge/consciousness) as the cognitive attainment that results from restoring malkhut. Da'at is defined as knowing that chesed and din are one (אחדות של חסד וגבורה) — not separating Hashem's mercy from His judgment. The intellectual oil (גרבי דמשחא = barrels of anointing oil = שכל/wisdom) is what the tzaddik draws down after cleaving to Ein Sof in the state of 'Ratzo veShov' (running and returning). The cluster includes: 'שמן משחת קדש' (holy anointing oil = sekhel), גרבי דמשחא (oil barrels = da'at), אחדות של חסד וגבורה (unity of mercy and judgment = da'at), שלא יחלק בין חסד לדין (not distinguishing between din and chesed = da'at). Merged into this package: יהוה/רחמים (Hashem's name = mercy — because knowing Hashem is the unifier of rachamim and din is the essence of da'at in this Torah); אחד/אהבה ('Echad' gematria = Ahavah / love — because God's oneness means that even din is love, the very definition of da'at in section 4 of the Torah).
merge_notes: Component 14 (יהוה, רחמים): The proof text states 'Hashem = rachamim' and links this to the core teaching that 'Hashem is One and His Name is One' — meaning both din and rachamim are one unity. This is the very definition of da'at as taught in section 4 of Torah #4: 'the essence of da'at is the unity of chesed and gevurot.' Merged by shared nature: divine attributes as unified da'at.

Component 19 (אחד, אהבה): 'Echad' gematria = Ahavah. The teaching is: 'Hashem is One and His Name is One' because He loves you — even din is love. This is the experiential content of da'at (knowing that all events are love). This concept bridges Packages 2 and 4, but its essential nature (the identity of oneness and love as the content of divine consciousness) places it more precisely in the da'at cluster. Merged by shared nature: the identity of oneness and love as cognitive-unifying da'at.

packages.label: אֵין סוֹף וְרְצוֹן — The Infinite and Its Will
packages.label_en: Ein Sof: The Infinite Will Behind All Wills
packages.reason: This small but conceptually pivotal cluster describes the highest divine level in Torah #4: אֵין סוֹף (the Infinite), whose essential nature is רְצוֹן (will/desire) — specifically the 'will of all wills' (רַעֲוָא דְּרַעֲוִין). The teaching holds that all individual divine wills (the shapes of letters = malkhut) receive their life-force from this single infinite simple will in which there is no change of will. The three nodes form a tight chain: אין סוף ↔ רעוא דרעוין ↔ רצון אין סוף. This is the divine 'pole' to which malkhut must be returned, and from which the tzaddik (Moshe, the bechina of Ayin) draws blessing when he cleaves in hitpashetut hagashmiyut (dissolution of corporeality). This cluster is the apex of the Torah's positive aspiration — the final destination of the malkhut-restoration process.

packages.label: יְדִיעָה שְׁלֵמָה — Complete Knowledge
packages.label_en: The Attainment of Knowing All Events Are for Good
packages.reason: This cluster captures the primary spiritual attainment taught at the opening of Torah #4: כְּשֶׁאָדָם יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכָּל מְאֹרְעוֹתָיו הֵם לְטוֹבָתוֹ (when a person knows that all his experiences are for his good). This knowing is called 'יְדִיעָה שְׁלֵמָה' (complete/perfect knowledge) and is equated with 'מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא' (a foretaste of the World to Come). The connection: today we bless good and bad with different blessings (hatov vehameitiv / dayan ha'emet), but in the future all will be hatov vehameitiv — meaning in the future state of consciousness, even apparent evil is recognized as good. This knowledge is the beginning and end of the Torah's teaching arc. It is distinct from the da'at package (Package 2) in that Package 2 describes the cognitive unity of chesed/din as divine attributes, while this package describes the personal experiential attainment of that knowledge in one's own life.

packages.label: חַד גַּלְגַּלָא דְּעֵינָא — The Single Eye of Mercy
packages.label_en: The Future Single Eye: Pure Goodness and Mercy
packages.reason: This compact cluster describes the Zoharic image of the messianic/future divine vision: 'חַד גַּלְגַּלָא דְּעֵינָא' (a single eye-ball of mercy), equated with 'כֻּלּוֹ הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב' (entirely the Good-and-Beneficent, the blessing of pure goodness) and 'עֵינָא חַד דְּרַחֲמֵי' (a single eye of mercy). In Torah #4, this is the messianic state that the tzaddik partially achieves when he cleaves to Ein Sof in hitpashetut: after returning (the 'shoov' of ratzo vaShov), he draws down this unified merciful gaze to illuminate his own da'at. This cluster is the good/evil mirror complement of the blindness and darkness of night-walking described in the parable (section 8). Where the parable-traveler fears thorns and pits in darkness, the attainment of the single eye of mercy sees only light.

packages.label: מִדּוֹת רָעוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע יְסוֹדוֹת — Evil Middot from the Four Elements
packages.label_en: The Evil Inclinations Rooted in the Four Physical Elements
packages.reason: This package is the good/evil mirror of Package 1 (malkhut and its repair). The Torah teaches that all evil middot (character flaws) derive from the four physical elements (יסודות) — earth/domem (producing sadness), plant/tzomea'ch (producing evil desires), animal/chai (producing idle speech), speaking-being/medaber (producing pride). These evil middot appear in the night-walking parable as the obstacles the traveler fears: קוצים (thorns) = צומח; פחתים (pits) = דומם; חיה רעה (evil beast) = חי; לסטים (bandits) = מדבר. The evil desires (גאוה, דברים בטלים) are the direct manifestations. The moon (ירח) governs all four sub-lunar elements, which are therefore called 'עבדים' (slaves) — the Egyptian slavery ('מבית עבדים') is a metaphor for bondage to these evil middot. The שרץ/טמאה pair (vermin/impurity) represents the spiritual impurity that mixes into prayer and disrupts divine service. This entire evil domain is what the three approaches to the tzaddik (seeing him, giving tzedakah, verbal confession) are designed to neutralize. Merged small components: Component 6a (דברים בטלים, חיה רעה, חי), Component 6b (גאוה, לסטים, מדבר), Component 7 (ירח, עבד), Component 8 (מדות רעות של ארבע יסודות, עבדים), Component 12 (פחתים, דומם), Component 13 (קוצים, צומח), Component 15 (שרץ, טמאה).
merge_notes: Component 6a (דברים בטלים, חיה רעה, חי): The element 'חי' produces the evil middot of idle speech (דברים בטלים) — these are the 'evil beast' (חיה רעה) in the parable. Kept as evil-elements cluster.

Component 6b (גאוה, לסטים, מדבר): The element 'מדבר' (speech capacity) produces pride (גאוה) — these are the 'bandits' (לסטים) in the parable. Same domain as Component 6a (evil middot from elements); merged into this evil package.

Component 7 (ירח, עבד): The moon (ירח) governs all four sub-lunar elements, and the Zohar calls it 'עבד' (slave). All four elements/middot are therefore 'עבדים' (slaves) — the Egyptian 'מבית עבדים' is a bechina of these evil middot. Merged into evil-elements package.
Component 8 (מדות רעות של ארבע יסודות, עבדים): Explicit statement that the four elements' evil middot are called 'עבדים'. Same proof text as Component 7. Merged into evil-elements package.

Component 12 (פחתים, דומם): 'Pits' = domem element = earth = source of sadness/depression. This is two of the four parable-obstacles directly equated with evil-element domains. Merged into evil-elements package.
Component 13 (קוצים, צומח): 'Thorns' = tzomea'ch element = plant = source of evil desires. Same structure as Component 12. Merged into evil-elements package.

Component 15 (שרץ, טמאה): The vermin (שרץ) in the whale's nostril = spiritual impurity (טמאה) that mixes into prayer and service. This is the evil domain that the three approaches to the tzaddik are designed to expel. While not directly from the four elements, it represents the evil force that infiltrates holy service — the enemy of Package 1's repair mechanism. Merged into evil-elements/impurity package.
